about: The plan (the source; PLAN.md is written from it). Edited only with node tools/plan.mjs. Dev reads it.
head:
# J Production · The World Plan

The one document of truth for the whole project: where it's going, what
holds always, every part of the world, what's being built now, what comes
next, what's parked and what's done. **Its eight parts never change** (shape
kept by `node tools/plan.mjs check`). Any request lands in one of them;
nothing ever adds another plan file. Details that *explain* how things work
live in the docs listed in part 8; they never hold plans or ticks.
chaptersIntro: *The fixed list. Every road and parked item sits under one of these.*

chapters.name: The world
chapters.what: what players see and do: the bar, avatars, games, people.
chapters.now: the bar is built and alive (three rooms, darts, chess, piano, 4K Mania, racing, bartending, jukebox, voice, profiles); the new light is live; frozen until J8, then remade item by item (J7 lays it out).

chapters.name: The site
chapters.what: the front door, the showcase, the news.
chapters.now: J Production's front page (Home, Projects, News) in Ember, with highlights pushed from Dev (R5); frozen until J8.

chapters.name: The engine
chapters.now: Looped: E1-E9 built (things with live loops, physics, sound, net), real light L1.1-L1.7 live, the tests' own lighting (J2.4); the script language is planned; paused until J8.

chapters.name: The tools
chapters.now: Dev (R4), the Studio, Dials, the UI Editor, Ember everywhere (R6); the restructure is giving the project its five books, honest checks and enforced procedures (J1-J8).

chapters.name: The backbone
chapters.now: accounts with ages, the ledger (credits), the multiplayer room, voice; accounts still on IONOS; both deploys report their real state to Dev (J2).

now.title: The Handbook
now.about: The Handbook: project and technology maps, every system, every data field, every page and button, every command, how-to recipes; the old notes sorted

pieces.text: The map of every folder (what it is, its language, who deploys it, its address) and of every language and outside tool
One page per system (about 40, one template: what it is, status, what you can do, how it works, data, commands, limits, checks, traps, history)
The data reference written from the files (the world's schema, theme tokens, screen parts, tools, the room protocol) and the world inventory (every thing, its model, what isn't placed)
Every page and control, by its exact label; a check that compares the pages' labels with the Handbook; the command list written from the front door
How-to recipes (about 25): each common request mapped to its exact steps
The old notes sorted (into the Handbook or the archive), decisions still in force recorded, duplicate pictures resolved, a docs check in the quick check

roadIntro: *Next and later, by chapter. Every item: a tag, what it is, the North star line it serves.*
upNext: J7 → J8 (the restructure; then the road as J7 orders it)

world.text: Alive avatars: breathing, blinking, looking at whoever talks, shifting weight, feet planted on stairs; one body with sliders.
Real people: skin light passes into, hair strands, wet see-through eyes, clothes that swing, lips that follow voice.
Your face: an avatar face from a few selfies.
Memory: the floor wears where people walk, the dartboard gets holes, your usual stool gets your nameplate.
Mood and chance: one cozy↔wild dial for the whole bar; "maybe" events (30% rain, a surprise band).
Time and era: scrub time back and see ghosts replay the night; a "what if" copy; the era dial (1920s ↔ neon future).
Scale and layers: shrink to mouse size; blend two places.
Home screen with "Happening now": start at your home, one tap to a busy hub, a live event or a friend.
Lobbies and matchmaking: a few main hubs (the bar first), instances, matching by age band, preferences and skill; the no-friends lobby.
Your home: invite-only, placing things on a smooth grid, expand up to 3x, levels 1-3.
Events and the memory book: date, time, RSVP, a clean invite card; the in-game camera, a photo book with likes, no comments, per-photo privacy.
Safety in the world: teens and adults kept apart (lobbies, voice, messages); block, mute, report (keeps the last seconds of voice); the teen phrase builder, filtered text for adults.
The mall, IKEA-style: walk in, pick things up, cart, checkout, delivery and install at home.
The casino: 18+, earned credits only, never bought or cashed out.
VIP marketplace (real money, its own place, unlocked forever by a first purchase; numbered, seasonal and event items) and trading (tradeable items only, a server-checked window and cooldown).
Small interactions done properly: bell, guitar, books, TV, door, taps.
Physics props: knock bottles off, glasses break and stack, pour drinks.
The pool table.
Room 3, taped off today (its question is still open).
Chess: bots with a chosen Elo, a menu to find a 1v1 or pick a bot.
Live low-res machine screens and a fair queue (20 s to claim your turn).
More arcade games; bots in two-player races.
Racing: the rigs' visual upgrade on the rebuilt track (waiting on your answer), then the driving rework stages (docs/DRIVING_REWORK.md).
Bodies that move right: stepping when turning on the spot, sit-down and stand-up motions, hands that really hold things, a face that moves when you talk.
Your own character builder (face, details); outfits and gadgets to show off (shop items).
The game screens remade in Ember after R6: HUD, 4K Mania and race screens, emote faces, the loading screen.
Remaster the crude first versions of props and rooms.

engine.text: Light leftovers: Air gets bounce strength and exposure range; the budget meter counts patches (lights in real units shipped in L1.7).

The engine phone check: fix every "broke" from the E1-E9 list; a ?perf=1 report by the fire with the mirror in view (against 63H3FJ, 16.7 ms); if reflections or shadows cost over 1 ms, make them cheaper.
Bug: the menu stops answering after some games.
Speed: three phone reports (after entering, at the mirror, after 2 min walking); faster drawing part 2 (render core, layout from Blender, quality settings).
Clean core leftovers: 4.1c, 4.3b, the darts / bartending / race adapters, entity ids on the wire.
Real surfaces: textures that never visibly repeat, rounded edges, automatic wear, dirt and smudges.
Shadows and shaped light: every light casts shadows, real lamp patterns (IES), lampshades that glow, fire that moves its shadows, contact shade.
The bar script language: parser, a tiny safe runner, errors with line numbers in the Studio; five behaviours rewritten as scripts.
Eyes and camera: smooth edges (TAA), white balance like the eye, seeing in the dark, glare and starbursts, film grain in the dark, focus.
Layers: varnish over wood, velvet and fabric sheen, brushed metal, wet surfaces.
Reflections and caustics: several reflection captures, screen reflections, light bounced off shiny things, caustics.
The air: haze and beams, dust in the light, smoke near the ceiling, heat shimmer.
Recipes: stool, chair, table, bottle, glass grown from recipes, every copy slightly different, dials in the Studio.
Light through things and real depth: subsurface (wax, skin, lampshades), glass with thickness, parallax depth; every model at real size.
Light show: theatre-style cues and light that is the music, as scripts; real bulb colours; a dying bulb.
Living light: a real sky through the windows (your time and weather), players carry light, neon afterglow.
Scan it: bring real things in with the iPhone camera.
Paint the light: brush warmth and shadow in the Studio; the engine places and tunes lamps to match.

CI's browser tests: since the new light (L1) the smoke test times out on GitHub's software GPU, so every test after it is skipped (the deploy itself still goes out); give CI a light-weight drawing mode and get every test running again

tools.text: The Studio phone check: fix every "broke S…"; a ?perf=1 report from the Studio with the Monitor open; the multiplayer test's late joiner (E3.6b) passing here too.
Engine flags in the Toolbelt: switch features (?light=classic, ?bounce=0 ...) without typing addresses.
The timeline: the Studio's centre strip (bar time, a track per thing, drag events on, loop them, scrub to preview), playing for everyone.
Launch: the check (rules, overlaps, blocked doors), bot players walk the draft, a report, then Launch with one-tap undo.
Claude in the Studio, live: Claude's edits stream into an open Studio one by one; you comment and press Launch.
The plan rebuilt with a reality check: a verdict on every item, the world remake laid out, the script language's realistic scope, the order
Proof, then unfreeze: cold-start drills with fresh AI sessions, a final audit, the first real job through the new system

backbone.text: Accounts off IONOS: logins move to the ledger's side, stronger password hashes, moved on first login.
The room checks chess moves and 4K Mania scores; then more games pay credits.
The room decides every shared thing (Phase 5).
Voice relays: TURN for strict networks, then a voice server (SFU) for big lobbies.
Safety on the server: age bands enforced, reports kept, blocks remembered.

parkedIntro: *Not on the road yet, by chapter. The user promotes them.*

world: The street and the city outside; homes there as your "real home".
A kids edition: a separate, simpler game in the same universe (under 13).
A new name for the world and its currency (Bar3D is a working name).
Mini music studio (a DAW in the bar).
Avatar from a face scan (the user's own character builder).
The street front: the bar seen from the street at night (front wall, lit door, people moving behind the windows, a street lamp), a new place in the world (was R5.5)
site: The front door scene running live in Looped instead of a clip (after R6, same places).
The front page's looping clip: the camera drifting to the bar's lit door, ~8 s, rendered from the engine, behind the intro (was R5.6)
engine: World-simulation engines: sound made from the physics, heat, smell as a field, day and night.
The engine checks itself: it notices when something isn't right (a thing out of place, a missing model, a broken loop) and helps say what and where (request 2026-10-24 #5)
tools: AI dock: a workspace on the site where you talk to Claude and it works on the project there.
AI inside the Studio (needs a paid API), importing your own models, mesh editing, several people editing at once.
A design for the Studio more like a 3D modelling room (the hub card "Design idea").
backbone: The site on Cloudflare Pages (unlocks threads in the game).

where:
*Docs that explain; they never hold plans or ticks.*
- `CLAUDE.md`: how a "go" runs. `docs/REFERENCE.md`: the long guide (layout, every tool, iOS limits).
- `docs/AUTOMATION.md`: the tools (piece, step, plan, uikit, studio, bench, gallery).
- `docs/ENGINE.md`: how Looped is built (things, loops, layers). `docs/STUDIO.md`: how the Studio works.
- `docs/manual/`: the manual (light, materials, recipes, timeline, world, avatars).
- `docs/PROTOCOL.md`: the multiplayer wire format. `docs/DRIVING_REWORK.md`: the driving spec.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: gotchas and why things are the way they are.
- `docs/archive/`: every old plan and progress file, kept to read, never to plan from.
